chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muawiya ibn Hukeym said:

Al-Rida (peace be upon him) delivered this sermon: All praise is for Allah who praised Himself in the Book, and opened His Book with praise, and made praise the first recompense for the abode of His bounty and the last call of the inhabitants of His Paradise. And I testify that there is no god except Allah, One, without a partner, a testimony I purify for Him and store with Him.

And Allah blesses Muhammad, the seal of prophethood and the best of creation, and his Progeny, the Progeny of mercy, the tree of bounty, the mine of messengership, and the destination of the angels. And praise is for Allah, who in His prior knowledge and speaking Book and truthful explanation, made the most rightful cause for kinship and preference, and the most deserving matter for desire, a cause that obligates a cause and a matter that results in self-sufficiency.
So He, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And it is He who created from water a human being and made for him lineage and marriage, and ever is your Lord Powerful.'

And He said: 'And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male slaves and your female slaves; if they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.'

And even if there were not in marriage and intermarriage a decisive verse, nor a followed sunnah, nor a widespread tradition, it would be among what Allah made of kindness to the near, bringing the distant close, uniting hearts, interlacing rights, increasing numbers, and providing offspring for the calamities of time and events of affairs, that which the wise intellect desires above it, the successful one hastens to it, and the educated one strives for it.

So the closest of people to Allah is he who follows His command, implements His ruling, fulfills His decree, and hopes for His reward. And So-and-so, son of So-and-so, whose state and majesty you know, was pleased with himself and came to you preferring you and choosing for the proposal of So-and-so, daughter of So-and-so, your noble one, and offered her such and such as dower. So receive him with acceptance and respond to him with desire, and seek Allah's guidance in your affairs, that He may strengthen you upon your right path, if Allah wills.

We ask Allah to join what is between you with righteousness and piety, to unite it with love and desire, and to seal it with harmony and pleasure. Indeed, He is the Hearer of supplication, Subtle to what He wills.

One of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fazzal, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said: 'I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying, then he mentioned the sermon just as Muawiya ibn Hukeym mentioned it, similar to it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for marriage proposals and intermarriage according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This sermon by Imam al-Rida (AS) serves as a practical juridical and spiritual guide for marriage, framing it not merely as a social contract but as an act of worship that fulfills divine command and strengthens communal bonds through 'mu'sarah' (intermarriage). The Imam highlights the theological significance of kinship ties (silat al-rahim) and social cohesion, urging the community to accept the proposal with gratitude and reliance on God (istikhara). It reflects the Shia emphasis on the Prophet's family as the model for righteous conduct and the integration of spiritual intention with social responsibility.
